title: Lifestyle Inflation: Why Your Raise Leaves You No Richer
description:
Lifestyle inflation is when spending rises as fast as your pay, so a raise leaves you no richer. In this example, a $5,000 raise is about $292 a month after tax. Spend it all on upgrades and you have nothing extra in 20 years; save half and invest it, and it could grow to about $76K, while you still enjoy the other half.

Example assumptions: $5,000 yearly raise, 30% combined tax on the extra pay (yours will differ), half of the after-tax raise ($145.83 a month) invested at the start of every month for 20 years at an assumed 7% average yearly return compounded monthly, no fees or taxes on the investment, no further raises. Illustration only: real returns vary, can be negative, and are not guaranteed. Not financial advice.

scenes.say: You get a five thousand dollar raise. Twenty years later, you could be no richer at all.
After an example thirty percent in taxes, you keep three thousand five hundred a year. Almost three hundred dollars a month.
Alex spends all of it. A nicer car, more takeout, a pricier phone plan. Sam saves half and enjoys the rest.
That's about one hundred forty-six dollars a month, invested at an assumed seven percent a year. Real returns vary.
Twenty years later, Sam has about seventy-six thousand dollars. Alex's upgrades just became normal life.
And Sam only put in thirty-five thousand of it. The rest is growth.
The fix is simple. Next time your pay goes up, raise your savings first, then upgrade with what's left.
